                    ### Question

                    ### Options

opb. Hyperflexibility, vision problems, and pneumothorax
opc. Systolic click auscultated on physical exam 10 years prior
opd. Repeated episodes of streptococcal pharyngitis as a child
ope. Cutaneous flushing, diarrhea, and bronchospasm

The patient's presentation of a systolic click after S2 followed by a rumbling murmur at the cardiac apex is highly suggestive of mitral valve prolapse. Further questioning should focus on a history of connective tissue disorders, such as Marfan syndrome, which can be associated with mitral valve prolapse. Evidence paths linking Marfan syndrome and connective tissue diseases to mitral valve prolapse support this association.
